title: Generic indicator-sum variance + subgraph thresholds in G(n, p)

problemStatement.formal: \text{Formalize a generic variance lemma for indicator sums }X = \sum_i X_i\text{ with }X_i\in\{0,1\}\text{, specialize it to subgraph counting in }G(n,p)\text{, and derive the canonical triangle threshold }p^*(n) = 1/n.
problemStatement.plain: The parent file ProbMethodSecondMoment.lean (227 lines, 0 sorries) ships abstract Chebyshev / Paley-Zygmund tools. OQ-02 asks for the application layer: a generic indicatorSum_variance lemma over indicator sums, a subgraphCount_variance specialisation, and the canonical triangle threshold p^*(n) = 1/n. Subcritical (p · n → 0) via Markov; supercritical (p · n → ∞) via Paley-Zygmund. S2 ACT estimated ~350 LOC into a new file ProbMethodSecondMomentOQ02.lean with 0-2 strategic sorries (the case-heavy Paley-Zygmund overlap-class calculation).
whyMatters: Closes the application gap: the gallery's abstract second-moment tools currently have no concrete random-graph application.
Threshold functions are the central result in random graph theory; a Lean-verified triangle threshold unlocks corollary stubs for every monotone subgraph property.
Mathlib upstreaming candidate: G(n, p) and the variance decomposition are missing from Mathlib v4.26.0.

builtItems: verify_triangle_threshold.py (2026-06-15) — EXACT certificate of the triangle second moment + threshold: overlap-class counts exhaustive (n=3..11); Var[X]=C(n,3)[p^3+3(n-3)p^5-(3n-8)p^6] proven == raw overlap-class E[X^2]-E[X]^2 (symbolic in n); brute-force enumeration of all 2^C(n,2) graphs matches E[X] and E[X^2] for n=3..6; at p=c/n, E[X]->c^3/6 (subcritical Markov) and Var/E^2->6/c^3 (supercritical Paley-Zygmund), pinning p*=1/n.
ProbMethodSecondMomentOQ02.lean (S2-A, merged #22687) — generic variance pair-sum decomposition Var(sum X)=sum Cov over t x t (Docker-verified, 0 sorries).
insights: For indicator sums, Var(X) = Σ μ_i(1 - μ_i) + Σ_{i≠j} Cov(X_i, X_j); the diagonal is bounded by E[X] (since X_i² = X_i), giving the classical second-moment bound.
Subgraph counts decompose by overlap class k = |E(H_i) ∩ E(H_j)|: terms with k = 0 (disjoint) have zero covariance and vanish; the dominant non-vanishing term often comes from k = 1.
For triangles, supercritical-side calculation: Var/E² ≈ 1/(n² p) → 0 in regime p · n → ∞, so Paley-Zygmund gives P[X ≥ 1] → 1.
G(n, p) is not in Mathlib v4.26.0; an ad-hoc product-measure definition (~30 LOC) suffices for the threshold derivation and is the natural Mathlib-upstreaming starting point.
mathlibGaps: G(n, p) random graph as a probability measure — entirely missing.
Variance over Finset (custom in parent; Mathlib's ProbabilityTheory.Variance is over MeasureTheory).
Standard subgraph-count threshold lemmas — none in Mathlib.
